updates.title: Microsoft Purview: Data Security Triage Agent – Sensitive Data Remediation
updates.summary: A new Data Loss Prevention function enables automated detection and remediation of sensitive data (SSNs, passwords, credit card numbers) across SharePoint and OneDrive at scale through Microsoft Teams integration. This reduces manual effort and compliance risk by allowing proactive identification and correction of policy violations across thousands of files.

updates.title: Microsoft Purview: Sensitivity Label Inheritance for Teams Meeting Artifacts
updates.summary: Teams meeting artifacts (recordings, transcripts, Loop notes) can now automatically inherit sensitivity labels from their parent meeting, ensuring consistent protection without manual labeling. This simplifies governance at scale and reduces the risk of unprotected content generation.

updates.title: Microsoft Purview: Insider Risk Management Alert Classification
updates.summary: Insider Risk Management now supports alert classification as True Positive, Benign (operational), or False Positive with predefined classification reasons, replacing existing dismissal reasons. This enables better risk reporting, alert tuning, and organizational risk posture management.

updates.title: Microsoft Purview: Auto-Label SharePoint Files to Library Defaults
updates.summary: Organizations can now automatically apply default sensitivity labels to existing SharePoint files based on their document library configuration, closing labeling gaps for data at rest. This enforces consistent, secure-by-default protection without relying on user action.

updates.title: Microsoft Purview: DLP and Auto-Labeling for Non-Microsoft Connected Apps
updates.summary: Data Loss Prevention and Information Protection auto-labeling now extend to non-Microsoft cloud services including Google Workspace, Box, Dropbox, Salesforce, ServiceNow, AWS, and Cisco Webex. This allows organizations to enforce consistent data protection policies across their entire cloud ecosystem.

updates.title: CVE-2026-118148: Active Directory Domain Services Elevation of Privilege
updates.summary: An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists in Active Directory Domain Services that could allow an attacker to gain higher privileges within the directory. Admins should review and apply available patches to maintain security posture.

updates.title: Microsoft Purview: Improved Sensitive Information Types
updates.summary: Microsoft is enhancing built-in sensitive information types (SITs) to detect sensitive data with greater precision and reliability. This improves the accuracy of DLP and auto-labeling policies, reducing false positives and false negatives.

updates.title: Microsoft Purview: Recurring Classifier Refresh
updates.summary: On-Demand Classification is evolving into recurring classification refreshes that automatically keep content classification current as organizational data and context change. This reduces manual effort and ensures classifications remain accurate over time.

updates.title: Microsoft Purview: Endpoint DLP Protection for Local AI Agents
updates.summary: Endpoint Data Loss Prevention now expands to protect sensitive data in AI agent interactions, including prompts, files, and tool interactions with local agents. Organizations can apply DLP policies to prevent sensitive data exposure as AI agents access and act on enterprise information.

updates.title: Microsoft Purview: Endpoint DLP Integration with Azure Firewall
updates.summary: Data Loss Prevention extends to the network layer through Azure Firewall integration, enabling detection and protection of sensitive data in network traffic from servers, VMs, and background services. This provides visibility and enforcement of DLP policies on traffic from applications and APIs.

updates.title: Microsoft Purview: Adaptive Scope Lifecycle Status Evaluation Control
updates.summary: Microsoft Purview Adaptive Scopes now provide explicit control over lifecycle-state evaluation for recipients and site owners, ensuring policy targeting remains aligned with organizational changes. This helps maintain accurate scope membership as employees and sites transition through their lifecycle.

updates.title: Microsoft Purview: Sensitivity Labels for Microsoft Entra Security Groups
updates.summary: Sensitivity labels can now be applied to Microsoft Entra cloud security groups using the same label configuration as Microsoft 365 groups and sites, without requiring separate setup. This extends consistent classification and governance across cloud-based group resources.

updates.title: CVE-2026-96082: Windows Kerberos Denial of Service Vulnerability
updates.summary: A denial of service vulnerability in Windows Kerberos could allow an attacker to disrupt authentication services. Organizations should monitor for available patches to protect their authentication infrastructure.

updates.title: CVE-2026-121680: Windows NTLM Spoofing Vulnerability
updates.summary: An NTLM spoofing vulnerability could allow an attacker to impersonate legitimate users or services in Windows authentication. This affects multiple products including Office, and admins should apply available updates to prevent exploitation.

updates.title: CVE-2026-105590: Active Directory Certificate Services Security Feature Bypass
updates.summary: Improper certificate validation in Active Directory Certificate Services allows an authorized attacker to bypass a security feature over the network. This could compromise certificate-based authentication and encryption mechanisms; admins should apply patches promptly.

updates.title: Microsoft Purview: Data Lifecycle Management – Azure PST Import
updates.summary: Azure PST Import enables migration of PST files from Azure Blob Storage directly into Exchange Online mailboxes using the standard Exchange Migration Service pattern. This simplifies large-scale mailbox migrations and supports data governance during transition.

updates.title: Microsoft Purview: Endpoint DLP – FTP and SFTP Transfer Monitoring
updates.summary: Endpoint Data Loss Prevention now monitors sensitive data transferred over FTP and SFTP protocols, allowing administrators to apply restrictive actions based on organizational policy. This extends DLP coverage to legacy file transfer protocols used throughout many enterprises.
